title: Global crop suitability datasets for 17 crops under present (2024) and future climate scenarios (2041–2100)
abstract: Accurately assessing crop suitability is essential for ensuring food security and guiding agricultural adaptation to climate change. However, existing suitability analyses are mainly based on empirical rules and coarse-resolution predictors, which limits their representativeness and prevents them from capturing contemporary global agricultural patterns with sufficient spatial detail. Here we propose a transferable novel framework that integrates crop samples from remote sensing-based crop layers and high-resolution environmental predictors to model the global suitability of 17 major crops, using the random forest model under present (2024) and future climate scenarios with a 1 km × 1 km resolution. The models achieve an overall accuracy exceeding 0.9 based on the independent test set. Compared with the Global Agro-edaphic suitability dataset from Global Agro-Ecological Zones-Model (GAEZ), our present suitability results show an improved accuracy, with a global pixel-level correlation coefficient (r) of 0.57, and strong agreement in classified suitability area comparisons (r = 0.99, R² = 0.97). This study offers valuable support for optimizing cropping patterns, enhancing agricultural resilience, and informing climate adaptation strategies.
problem: Existing crop suitability analyses are limited by empirical rules and coarse-resolution predictors, which restricts their representativeness and ability to capture contemporary global agricultural patterns with sufficient spatial detail.
method: The paper proposes a novel framework that integrates remote sensing-based crop samples and high-resolution environmental predictors to model the global suitability of 17 major crops for present and future climate scenarios using a random forest model.
task: The task is to generate high-resolution global suitability datasets for 17 crops under present and future climate scenarios using a random forest model trained on remote sensing-based crop samples and environmental predictors.
innovation: This paper presents a novel framework that integrates remote sensing crop samples with high-resolution predictors and a random forest model to generate 1 km global suitability datasets for 17 major crops under present and future climate scenarios, showing improved accuracy over existing datasets.

kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: The main objectives are (1) to evaluate the accuracy and effectiveness of the crop suitability modeling approach that integrates crop samples and predictors derived from remote sensing and reanalysis data and random forest, and (2) to generate 1 km spatial resolution distribution maps of crop suitability for 17 crops under present (2024) and three future periods (2041-2060, 2061-2080, 2081-2100) under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs: SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5). This updated crop suitability dataset is expected to contribute to the optimization of cropping systems, improvement of crop yields, and sustainability of ecology. For future climate scenarios, since TerraClimate and GLEAM do not provide future projections, the corresponding predictors were replaced by simulated data from WorldClim59 and Phase 6 of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP6)60.

kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: A two-part validation procedure, which comprises model accuracy validation and suitability results assessment was employed. For model accuracy validation, 25% of the sample set was used during cross-validation and ultimately as the independent test set to assess the performance of the random forest model for each crop. Evaluation indices include F1-score, overall accuracy, producer's accuracy, and user's accuracy for both positive and negative classes.
